docs.title: 0.7.0 — Chimera
docs.text:
Theme: Linux x86_64 target (Python backend).

Linux support moves up the timeline. It is independent of the language-model work below, it gives the project native Linux CI early, and the audit found the target-independent portion of the compiler is large (lexer, parser, semantic analysis, FIR/FLIR, the assembler core, most of flir_to_asm). Only the self-hosted tooling (elf_writer.fire) stays later, in 0.12.0.

docs.title: Python backend support
docs.text:
• Add an ELF64 writer under backend/linux/elf.py (mirrors backend/windows/pe.py): a static executable with no imports and a _start entry point
  • Add a Linux runtime-extern table under firescript/platforms/linux.py (mirrors firescript/platforms/windows.py), wired into flir/lowering.py for the Linux target
  • Add a System V AMD64 calling convention to codegen/x86_64/flir_to_asm.py alongside the existing Win64Convention, selected per-target (rdi/rsi/rdx/rcx/r8/r9, no shadow space, 16-byte stack alignment); update the register assumptions in the fs_rt_mem_copy thunk and the stack-argument offsets
  • Replace the Windows entry sequence with a _start that reads argc/argv from the stack, calls the entry function, and exits via exit_group
  • Add a syscall instruction to the assembler and an FLIR intrinsic that lowers to mov rax, n; syscall
  • Runtime: a Linux layer under std/internal — heap via mmap/brk, I/O and file operations via raw syscalls (read, write, open, close, unlink, rename, lseek/fstat, exit_group), and process arguments from the initial stack. main.py currently compiles every std/internal/*.fire file into every program, with the win_* externs inside them, so the runtime sources must become per-target
  • main.py selects the writer and output suffix per target (no .exe on Linux)
  • Add Target(Platform.LINUX, Arch.X86_64) to SUPPORTED_TARGETS in firescript/targets.py (already selectable on the CLI via --platform linux --arch x86_64, since the choices mirror the full README support matrix — this just wires up the backend)
  • firescript-on-Linux CI (GitHub Actions) runs the golden suite under a native Linux build
  • Update tests/run.py's run kind / matrix engine to support cross-target testing

docs.title: Test coverage
docs.text:
• ELF validity checks (readelf or a pure-Python ELF inspector) on Linux target builds
  • Linux target golden suite runs on CI (native Linux)
  • Cross-target tests: the same source produces equivalent output on both targets
  • Fuzzing and edge-case infrastructure, phase 1 (see testing_plan.md): the fuzz test kind with minimization, the error-code coverage check, PYTHONHASHSEED determinism variation, numeric-boundary matrices, and the regex / collection oracles

docs.title: Gate
docs.text: --platform linux --arch x86_64 produces a working native ELF binary for all test sources, and both targets pass their golden suites on CI.

docs.title: 0.8.0 — Basilisk
docs.text:
Theme: Memory and safety model.

Replaces the Owned/Copyable model with value semantics: every type is a value, copying is the default, moving and borrowing are explicit. Also delivers const enforcement and member visibility. Full design: language_model_redesign.md §1–§4.

This release deliberately precedes self-hosting. The Python compiler is the only implementation right now; reworking the model before the self-hosted front-end and backend are written avoids writing them twice.

docs.title: Language features
docs.text: Feature Rationale Memberwise copy by default; explicit move; first-party deep-copy hook Predictable value semantics like C++; the Owned/Copyable categories disappear from user code. Inline class layout (classes are values, not implicit heap pointers) Required by value semantics and by the performance goal. &T / &mut T as real reference types with exclusive &mut Memory safety without runtime checks. Elided-lifetime returns allowed; no reference fields yet. const enforcement: binding const, transitive const through &T, const fields const is currently parsed but not enforced. private / protected / public on class members Encapsulation; no member visibility exists today. Removal of copyable class, CopyableOption/CopyableResult/CopyablePair, and the planned Owned/Copyable generic constraints One kind of value; no duplicated stdlib types.

docs.title: Compiler improvements
docs.text:
• Consolidate move/drop logic (currently duplicated in semantic_analyzer.py, preprocessor.py and the FIR ownership verifier) into one source of truth before changing the rules
  • Change class lowering from heap-pointer to inline layout in FIR/FLIR
  • Derive trivially copyable / needs destructor / copyable internally; derive the destructor for ArrayList-style types from field types instead of @owns_elements
  • Implement &T as a type, exclusivity checking over lexical scope, and the elided-return rules
  • Enforce const and read-only access through &T
  • Enforce that compiler directives are usable only from the standard library
  • Rewrite docs/reference/memory_management.md, docs/glossary.md and the other docs that use the Owned/Copyable terms (see the migration notes in the design document); resolve the doc/implementation drift listed there

docs.title: Test coverage
docs.text:
• Intentional, documented update of the memory tests that encode the old model
  • Golden and error tests for copy, move, use-after-move, move-only types, &/&mut exclusivity, reference-return rules, const, and visibility
  • Regression tests for the unified Option / Result / Pair
  • Ownership and borrowing fuzzer plus the runtime allocation counter (see testing_plan.md)

docs.title: Gate
docs.text: No Owned/Copyable terminology remains in the language or docs. Copy, move, borrow, const and visibility rules are enforced by the compiler and covered by tests. All existing programs that are still valid under the new model pass; any change to a test's expectations is documented in the changelog.

docs.title: 0.9.0 — Manticore
docs.text:
Theme: Object model and standard library architecture.

Java-style OOP that compiles to flat, statically dispatched code, and a standard library built on it. Full design: language_model_redesign.md §5–§9.

docs.title: Language features
docs.text: Feature Rationale Interfaces, with static dispatch by default and &Interface for dynamic dispatch Abstraction over AST node types, type representations and backends; Comparable, Iterable, Hashable. Abstract classes Java-style class hierarchies. Object root class, with vtable pointers only where dynamic dispatch needs them and whole-program devirtualization A single related hierarchy without a universal per-object cost. Primitive bindings (@bind, std-only), with implicit import, and Integer as an interface for generic <T: Integer> a.abs() on an int32; accept any precision with type safety. Function interfaces (interface fn) and non-capturing lambdas Contracts on callable parameters. Conversion methods on bindings replace the as keyword; contains replaces in-membership; isInstance<T>() / isExactly<T>() / downcast<T>() on Object Fewer keywords, explicit conversion semantics, fallible parsing via Result. See design doc §8. Box<T> and Shared<T> Recursive types, owned polymorphism and dynamic lifetime. Lowest priority in this release; may slip. Capturing and escaping closures Depend on exclusivity and Box. Lowest priority; may slip. Exceptions raised by language operations (overflow, division by zero, bounds, invalid casts) as catchable Exception extends Object subclasses with try / catch / finally; fallible function calls return Result; debug-build stack traces Python-style error handling consistent with the safety model. See design doc §9. Generic enums and Option<T> as enum { Some(T), None }, matched with match; Some/None infer type arguments from the expected type; null and T? removed One way to express absence, explicit and composable (nests, usable as a generic argument). Needs inline storage or a compact representation for small enums so Option<int32> does not allocate. See design doc §12. Improved error messages / diagnostic infrastructure The firescript compiler should produce rich, helpful diagnostics; implementing this in firescript requires the same.

docs.title: Compiler improvements
docs.text:
• Interface and abstract-class parsing, semantic checking, and FIR/FLIR lowering (monomorphized static dispatch, vtables only where needed, devirtualization of non-overridden methods)
  • Replace the parse-time copy-down inheritance with real subtyping
  • Binding table (type to class) with deterministic implicit module loading; generalize @builtin_method beyond the string and array families
  • Function-type syntax, signature matching, and lambda lowering (non-capturing first)
  • Initial standard library abstractions modeled on Java: Object, Comparable<T>, Iterable<T>, Hashable, Equatable, Printable; migrate HashMap<K,V> off its fixed hashable-type set onto Hashable

docs.title: Test coverage
docs.text:
• Golden tests for interfaces, abstract classes, Object, bounds on generic functions, and dispatch (static and dynamic)
  • Tests that unoverridden methods are devirtualized and that vtables are emitted only where needed
  • Binding tests (implicit import, every integer width, generic Integer bound)
  • Function-interface and lambda golden and error tests
  • Generated tests for dispatch, interface bounds, and bindings (see testing_plan.md)

docs.title: Gate
docs.text: Interfaces, abstract classes, Object, primitive bindings, and function interfaces work across the full pipeline, and the standard library collections use the new abstractions. The language is mature enough to begin writing a compiler front-end.

docs.title: 0.10.0 — Wyvern
docs.text:
Theme: FCL configuration system.

With collections, regex and the object model in place, this release delivers FCL — the config language that kiln will use for package manifests.

docs.title: FCL
docs.text:
FCL (firescript config language) is a typed configuration DSL that kiln will use for package manifests and project configuration. It is a mini-compiler: lexer, parser, typechecker, and (eventually) interpreter. Implementing FCL in firescript serves as a crucible for the self-hosting work in 0.11.0 — the same patterns (enums for tokens/AST, recursive-descent parsing, interface-based visitors) are exercised here at smaller scale before tackling the full firescript compiler.

  • Lexer (tokenizer) — builds on the existing std/fcl/lexer.fire stub
  • Parser — recursive-descent over FCL syntax, producing typed AST (enum-based)
  • Typechecker — validates structure against expected types
  • Runtime interpreter — evaluates FCL expressions and produces config values
  • Compile-time import support for .fcl files in firescript source
  • Document .fcl format and FCL import mechanism

docs.title: Compiler improvements
docs.text: • Implement FCL pipeline in the firescript compiler (recognize .fcl imports, invoke FCL interpreter, merge results into the FIR module)

docs.title: Test coverage
docs.text:
• Comprehensive FCL golden tests (valid config files produce expected output)
  • FCL error tests (invalid config syntax, type mismatches, missing values)
  • End-to-end tests for .fcl imports in firescript source

docs.title: Gate
docs.text: FCL is usable: valid .fcl files produce correct config values; invalid ones report clear diagnostics. The compiler can import and consume FCL configuration.

docs.title: 0.11.0 — Dragon
docs.text:
Theme: Self-hosted compiler front-end.

Write the firescript compiler's front-end (lexer, parser, semantic analysis, FIR construction) in firescript. The Python compiler remains the bootstrap compiler; the firescript front-end is developed alongside it and tested against the same test suite.

docs.title: firescript/std/compiler/lexer.fire
docs.text:
• Token type definitions (enum-based)
  • Source text → token stream conversion
  • Character classification, string/number literal lexing, keyword recognition
  • Error reporting with source locations

docs.title: firescript/std/compiler/parser.fire
docs.text:
• Recursive-descent parser producing AST nodes (enum-based)
  • Expression, statement, type, and declaration parsing
  • Operator precedence handling
  • Error recovery / syntax error reporting

docs.title: firescript/std/compiler/semantic.fire
docs.text:
• Scope and binding analysis

docs.title: 0.12.0 — Behemoth
docs.text:
Theme: Self-hosted backend and bootstrap (Windows and Linux).

Write the code generator (FLIR lowering, assembly emission) and the self-hosted toolchain (assembler, PE writer, ELF writer) in firescript. The firescript compiler compiles itself end-to-end on Windows x86_64 and Linux x86_64 (the Linux target exists in the Python backend since 0.7.0).

docs.title: firescript/std/compiler/codegen.fire
docs.text:
• FIR → FLIR lowering (monomorphization, class lowering, generator lowering)
  • FLIR → x86-64 assembly text emission
  • Support for all FLIR ops the Python backend emits (must achieve byte-identical assembly)

docs.title: firescript/std/compiler/assembler.fire
docs.text:

  • Object image production (sections, symbols, relocations)

docs.text:

  • Must produce byte-identical output to Python backend/windows/pe.py

docs.title: firescript/std/compiler/elf_writer.fire
docs.text:
• Pure-firescript ELF64 writer for Linux x86_64
  • ELF header, program headers, section headers, symbol table, relocation handling
  • Must produce byte-identical output to Python backend/linux/elf.py
  • Linux x86-64 syscall ABI and System V AMD64 calling convention in the firescript codegen

docs.title: Bootstrap
docs.text:
• python firescript/main.py --compiler firescript toggle uses the firescript compiler (front-end + backend) end-to-end
  • The firescript compiler compiles itself: python firescript/main.py --compiler firescript firescript/std/compiler/... produces a working firescript compiler binary
  • First-stage bootstrap: use the resulting binary to compile itself again: ./build/compiler.exe firescript/std/compiler/... produces a byte-identical binary (or semantically equivalent)
  • Document the bootstrap procedure in docs/internal/development/bootstrap.md

docs.text: python firescript/main.py --compiler firescript <file>.fire produces a working binary for any test source (Windows x86_64 and Linux x86_64). The firescript compiler can compile itself end-to-end. The resulting binary, when run on the firescript compiler sources, produces a byte-identical (or semantically equivalent) copy of itself.

docs.title: 0.14.0 — Leviathan

Theme: std.net + kiln networking.

Leviathan is the primordial sea beast — the vast network ocean. This release delivers networking primitives and connects kiln to the world with registry support.

docs.title: 1.0.0 — Titan
docs.text:
Theme: Stabilization, polish, and release.

With the compiler self-hosted, running on both Windows and Linux, the full kiln toolchain available, and the standard library covering networking, the 1.0.0 release focuses on making firescript production-ready and retiring the Python compiler.

docs.title: Language and stdlib stabilization
docs.text:
• Finalize all language features for 1.0 (no breaking changes after this); this assumes the memory model (0.8.0) and object model (0.9.0) have shipped — see language_model_redesign.md
  • Complete standard library documentation across all modules
  • Performance profiling and optimization of the self-hosted compiler

docs.text:

  • Remove --frontend flag (long superseded)
  • Remove Python test-runner dependency: test runners rewritten in firescript or kept as lightweight Python wrappers with no compiler logic
  • firescript compiler source becomes the canonical implementation

docs.title: Release criteria
docs.text:
1. firescript compiler is fully self-hosted — compiles itself end-to-end with no Python compiler code invoked in the compile path
  2. 100% test suite passes on the self-hosted compiler across both target platforms
  3. Compiler runs on Windows x86_64 (Tier 1) and Linux x86_64 (Tier 1, CI-tested every commit)
  4. kiln provides init, build, run, test, publish, add, sync, update
  5. Standard library is documented, stable, and tested (std.collections, std.text, std.types, std.io, std.math, std.fs, std.regex, std.fcl, std.ranges, std.cli.args, std.net)
  6. Changelog is complete; migration guide documents any breaking changes from 0.x
  7. No feature in docs/ carries [IN DEVELOPMENT]; [PLANNED] items are explicitly marked for post-1.0
  8. The Python compiler is removed; python firescript/main.py is a thin shim or gone
  9. A nightly fuzz run (see testing_plan.md) completes with no open crashers
