docs.title: 4. Docs vs compiler conflicts needing an owner decision
docs.text:
For each: what conflicts, then option A (change the compiler/tests) and option B (change the docs/status marker).

ID Conflict Option A Option B Tests affected D01 Integer overflow: type_system.md L141-153 and error_handling.md L31-38 say overflow traps at runtime (compile error for constants). Compiler wraps silently (S3 #1, S4 B3). Implement trap (+ constant-overflow error); move wrap tests to known_issues, add a trap test. State wraparound semantics in the docs; keep the wrap tests but label them as defined behavior; keep constant-overflow error (B45). types_int8, types_uint8, edge_cases_overflow_underflow, stress_integer_overflow D02 Out-of-range array index: arrays.md says runtime error; compiler reads garbage. Initializer size mismatch: docs say Error, compiler accepts (B23). Add bounds check (runtime) and compile-time size-mismatch error. Document unchecked access (UB) and relax size rule. none today; invalid/arrays/array_errors comments D03 Nested arrays: arrays.md:118-131 ("not fully implemented", old int8[3][3] matrix syntax) has no [PLANNED] marker (CLAUDE.md requires one); compiler rejects "Array literals cannot directly contain arrays" (3 tests pin it). Implement nested arrays. Add [PLANNED] marker and update syntax in the doc. invalid/types/type_mismatches, invalid/arrays/array_edge_invalid, invalid/types/cast_and_generic_type_errors D04 & intersection / interface constraints are [PLANNED] (type_system.md), but parsed as a union (B32). Reject & with a diagnostic until implemented; add invalid known-issue test. Implement intersection semantics and interfaces. 3 intersection run tests (delete), manifest line ~634 D05 Undocumented builtins: toInt/toFloat/toDouble/toBool/toChar/toString (only a v0.x changelog mention; parser/type_system.py:873), plus i32_to_f64/f64_to_i32/i32_to_str (listed in ast_to_fir.py). toChar("65") -> '6' vs toChar(66) -> 'B' is inconsistent. Remove/deprecate; delete their tests. Document them; fix toChar inconsistency. builtin_conversions, builtin_conversions_numeric_source, stress_type_conversions, stress_string_operations, string_cast_test D06 Receiver-less methods: instance methods without a receiver that use this, and receiver-less ctors, compile and behave as instance methods; classes.md says receivers required and static needs static fn. Also owned this ctor (vs memory_management.md saying consuming this is [PLANNED]), &this ctor (docs say ctors take &mut this), undocumented Type.Type(args) ctor form. Reject with a diagnostic; rewrite the large receiver-less slice of invalid/classes/*. Document the forms. classes_static_methods, memory_implicit_receiver_borrow, classes_owned_this_constructor, classes_constructor_owned_borrowed_param, invalid/classes/{instance_method_*,super_call_*,constructor_call_*,field_access_*}, type_method_call_constructor_form (both dirs) D07 Copyable-class field rule (classes.md: all fields of a copyable class must be Copyable) is unenforced; copyable class Pair<T,U> with string compiles (and the docs' own example uses it). Possible double-free of the string on bit-copy (not observed). Enforce; add invalid test; switch generics_class_basic / generics_class_inferred_construct string instantiations to an owned class. Relax the rule for generics (T Copyable-only at instantiation) and document. the two generic-class run tests D08 docs/reference/std/math.md says nested generic calls fail to compile ("known limitation"); math_abs_min_max_clamp nests them and passes (S5). Doc fix only. n/a none D09 enum/match have no reference page (only changelog; CLAUDE.md status table says IMPLEMENTED). Statement-position expression-bodied match arms work (enum_body_formatting) but changelog says statement arms use {}. Write the reference page and document/forbid expression arms in statements. Leave changelog as the spec; move the test to a documented form. enum_body_formatting, invalid/enums/*, invalid/match/* D10 Unsuffixed literals take the declared type (type_system.md:102-112, and x: int8 = 200 error at :114); compiler rejects all of them (B42). Implement contextual literal typing + range check. Require suffixes in docs. invalid/types/semantic_modulo_mismatch D11 Cyclic import detection marked [IMPLEMENTED] (imports.md:159) but dead (B24). Fix _load_module ordering; test FS-IMP-0002. Change marker to [IN DEVELOPMENT] / remove claim. import_cycle_a and 2 Python tests D12 scoping.md ("functions have access to global variables", section 6 [IMPLEMENTED]) vs ICE (B04); top-level use-before-declaration listed as error (scoping.md:259-262) vs accepted (B43). Implement/diagnose. Edit docs / status. scoping_function (delete) D13 Literal overflow compile-time error (type_system.md:117,150-153) vs accepted (B45); \q invalid escape: string keeps the backslash (string_escape_edge_cases, documented as intentional in its header) while char '\d' -> 'd' (char_type); no diagnostic either way. Diagnose. Document the lenient escapes. literal_errors, char_type, string_escape_edge_cases D14 Brace-less if/while: docs control_flow.md:7 say braces; tests exist and compiler accepts (control_flow_braceless*). Reject. Document braceless bodies (and decide the EOF-dangling if). control_flow_braceless, _if_at_eof, for_in_braceless_body, unterminated_if_body D15 Fall-off-the-end return unspecified (B10). Missing-return diagnostic (known_issue exists for bare return;). Document implicit-zero (and fix the string ICE). 3 fallthrough tests D16 fn main entry semantics and "top-level statements ignored when main exists, with a WARNING" appear in no reference doc; tests rely on it. Document. Reconsider the behavior. function_main_ignores_top_level, imports_alias D17 Entry definition vs import conflict: imports_entry_shadow pins entry wins; build_merged_ast docstring says conflict "produces an error"; Python tests pin the opposite fallback (B25). Pick: error, or entry-wins; make code, docstring, tests agree. imports_entry_shadow, 3 Python tests D18 Float -> int out-of-range/NaN/inf semantics undefined (B21); docs say "may truncate". Define (saturate / trap) and test. Document as unspecified and drop the out-of-range lines from int_float_cast_matrix. int_float_cast_matrix D19 String/array behaviors pinned but undocumented: .size() on arrays (arrays_length_param), array as string format (array_to_string), println(array) = [...] (B19), substring clamping, string parse leniency ("+7", "1e3"), byte-based length() on UTF-8, NUL truncation. Specify and test or restrict. Document as-is. those tests, strings_unicode, strings_index_of_substring D20 Borrow rules: memory_management.md marks read-only/non-retainable borrows [IMPLEMENTED] but holes exist (B38); moves in loop bodies unspecified (B39); re-initialization after move unspecified. Close the holes. Narrow the docs. invalid/borrow/* D21 Implicit constructors (Point(x,y) field constructor, NoCtor() allowed, new NoCtor(5) rejected) undocumented in classes.md. Document and make new consistent. Forbid. class_static_method_errors l.15 relies on it D22 % integer-only is not stated in operators.md (used by compound_assignment_type_errors); type-parameter % accepts floats (B54a). Document integer-only. Allow floats. compound_assignment_type_errors, generics_modulo_type_param D23 Nullable -> non-nullable: variables.md only says "cannot be assigned null" (B46). Check. Document. nullable_errors D24 Spec parity: P3 notes FLIR spec M4 (slot-propagated strconst store) and M2 (raw-pointer alignment) are stricter than the verifier; FIR spec S6 says every named type must resolve but a test pins leniency; type_system.md claims correct rounding/subnormals/NaN for float128 and float128.md claims fuzz validation vs the oracle that is not committed; types.md (std types doc) says all std types are tested but CopyablePair has no direct test. Tighten verifier/add tests. Document the narrowing in spec 8.x / soften claims. test_heap_verifier_checks::test_m4_store_through_slot_loaded_string_literal_alias_is_not_resolved, test_verifier_checks::test_m1_access_through_raw_pointer_is_not_checked, test_verifier_structural_and_method_call::test_s6_array_element_type_unresolved

Also decide (small): whether typeof legacy checks stay (B50) and the error codes for return/yield mismatches (S9: FS-SEM-0002 may fit better than FS-SEM-0010) before the known_issue checks are written; whether known_issues should pin @col.

docs.title: 5.0 Cross-shard conflicts: delete only ONE side
docs.text:
Reports in different shards each called the other copy the keeper. Deleting both would lose the coverage.

docs.title: 6. Recommended order of operations and risk notes
docs.text:
1. Safe first: duplicate deletions (5.1/5.2 DELETE columns marked REDUNDANT with a named surviving copy; Python DELETE for exact duplicates). Resolve table 5.0 first so you never delete both sides. Update tests/TEST_MANIFEST.md in the same commit (e.g. line ~634 for the intersection tests; sections for performance/ and edge_cases/).
  2. Fix the currently failing test (invalid/operators/operator_errors.fire line 60 annotation) in its own commit; it needs no compiler change.
  3. Fix wrong-reason compile-fail tests (add import @firescript/std.io.println;, drop cascade annotations, rewrite obsolete syntax, split comprehensive files, move un-annotated scenarios to known_issues). Do not drop cascade annotations if the harness requires every diagnostic to be annotated (S8 asked "if harness allows"): verify first.
  4. Fix weak run tests (sentinel lines for the trailing-blank-line harness behavior, %f-hiding comparisons, snapshot directives for drop tests, heap-payload tests). Expected values listed in the reports were verified to pass today unless marked "fails until B0x".
  5. Add missing coverage and known-issue tests (5.4). Tests that expose bugs go to known_issues, not to normal directories (CLAUDE.md "Never Skip Tests": they must fail loudly, with a header comment).
  6. Fix compiler bugs, then move the corresponding known-issue test (and the tests that pin the buggy behavior, theme 7) to correct expectations in the same commit as the fix (CLAUDE.md: bug fix includes its regression test). Highest value first: ICEs and silent wrong results (B01-B24), then the borrow/diagnostic holes.
  7. Decide the doc conflicts (section 4) before touching the tests they affect (D01, D06, D07, D10, D05 gate many deletions). Doc changes update [IMPLEMENTED]/[IN DEVELOPMENT]/[PLANNED] markers in the same commit.
  8. Python cleanup last, after the owner's policy call on contrived dead-guard tests; delete production dead code and its tests together; run the full suite between steps.

Risk notes: - Never edit expectations just to pass (CLAUDE.md). The only legitimate expectation edits here are where an intentional, documented behavior change occurred (operator_errors line 60) or where the test pins a bug and the bug is being fixed. - One logical change per commit (CLAUDE.md): each cleanup area (or each deleted cluster) its own commit; user-facing changes (diagnostics, new errors, doc markers) update docs/changelog.md under "Currently in Development"; do not bundle test cleanup with compiler fixes. - Deleting a test that carries a snapshot (arrays_iteration_for_in, generics_modulo_type_param, types_int64) loses the snapshot: move the //@ snapshot: directive first; snapshot files live in tests/snapshots/<category>/. - Deleting "regression" tests (imports_symbol_alias, option_issome_isnone, strings_for_in_regression_*) is a judgment call; the reports mark them "soft". - Deleting dead-guard Python tests lowers line coverage; coverage is a diagnostic, not a target (CLAUDE.md), but confirm no coverage gate exists. - Some audited claims are not independently verified: "no other test covers X" claims rest on grep, not semantic analysis (S1, S3); snapshot content was not reviewed; native-Windows behavior unverified (wine only, S3); whether the harness picks up a run-kind known_issues/ directory; header claims in the 11 known_issues files about FIR/FLIR verifier errors (S9). The P3 report notes a sibling's FIR-mutation script was accidentally run in P3's private copy (no effect on the repo). - Wine/Linux runs only; native Windows or other targets not exercised.

docs.title: Policy note (applies to every *dead_guards* / *_internals / *_coverage file)
docs.text: CLAUDE.md says: 'Line coverage is a diagnostic ... defensive or unreachable lines don't need contrived tests.' Roughly 100 of the 218 tests do exactly that: they monkeypatch consume, hand-build ASTNodes, bypass ASTNode's None-guard, or swap the lexer regex purely to execute a line no source can reach. Their only effect is to freeze dead code in place. Recommended: delete the tests, and (where the maintainer is certain it is dead) the guards. A second systemic problem: tests/python/parser/test_type_system_dead_guards_more.py does from _helpers import ... WITHOUT inserting its own directory in sys.path; it only imports because another module loaded earlier did the insert (running that file alone in a fresh interpreter raises ModuleNotFoundError; I hit this when running tests individually; the harness discovers/imports all modules in one process so it passes there). Also three different helper modules (_helpers, _dead_guard_helpers, _dead_guard_helpers2) duplicate each other.

docs.title: Compiler bugs discovered (all reproduced in the private copy)
docs.text:
1. Cyclic-import detection is dead code. imports.py _load_module checks dotted in self.modules (and returns) before the dotted in load_stack check, and sets self.modules[dotted]=mod before recursing, so a real A<->B cycle never raises CyclicImportError (FS-IMP-0002). docs/reference/imports.md:159 says [IMPLEMENTED] Cyclic import detection. Repro: python firescript/main.py --check tests/sources/invalid/imports/import_cycle_a.fire prints "Variable 'ping' not defined" (FS-PARSE-0003) attributed to import_cycle_b_provider.fire:2:40 - a symptom, which tests/sources/invalid/imports/import_cycle_a.fire currently pins as the expected output.
  2. Duplicate top-level symbol conflicts are only logged, never fail the compile. Repro: a.fire and b.fire each export fn shared() -> int32, main.fire import a.shared; import b.shared; println(shared()); compiles and produces an exe (first wins), stderr shows [ERROR] Conflicting top-level symbol 'shared' from imports. Same for an entry-defined fn shared() shadowing an import ("Top-level symbol 'shared' in entry conflicts with imported symbol"): exe produced. build_merged_ast's docstring says conflicts 'produce an error'.
  3. Constructor with a borrowed regular param plus an owned param mis-assigns ownership. Repro: class Inner{v:int32; fn Inner(&mut this, v:int32){this.v=v;}} class Outer{total:int32; fn Outer(&mut this, &a: Inner, owned b: Inner){this.total=a.v+b.v;}} x:Inner=Inner(1); y:Inner=Inner(2); o:Outer=Outer(x,y); println(o.total); -> FIRV-O2 in main: use of 'x', which is moved (internal compiler error). (test_parser_base.py::test_constructor_with_borrowed_and_owned_regular_params_parses comment hints at this.) Likely receiver/param index misalignment in ctor borrow flags.
  4. Bare arr[0]; statement and a directive x; inside a function body are accepted by the parser but crash AST->FIR with FIRConversionError: Unsupported statement node ARRAY_ACCESS|DIRECTIVE (Python traceback printed). Pinned as 'works' by test_statements_coverage.py.
  5. Nested generic class instantiation as a type argument (nested: Pair<Pair<int32,int32>,int32> = Pair(Pair(1,2),3);) fails FLIR verification FLIRV-T4 ("argument 0 has type i32, expected ptr"); still reproducible; not in tests/sources/**/known_issues (only invalid/known_issues exists).
  6. (Possible, unverified end-to-end) type_system.py:~950 not hasattr(node,'return_type') is never True because ASTNode always defines return_type; if the parser ever leaves return_type None for a user function call the fallback lookup in self.user_functions is skipped. The test that reaches it (..fallback_assignment_is_dead) pins that.
  7. Missing coverage for reachable behavior (not bugs): 'Cannot borrow Copyable type' (fn f(&x: int32)), match arms mixing enums / unknown enum, fn foo {} and fn + () ... (missing '(' / missing name) have no tests/sources compile-fail fixtures; the only coverage is the Python unit tests above.

Ran two mutation campaigns in private copies (never the shared repo; no git changes): (a) every emit("FIRV-x")/Violation("FIRV-x") line relabelled to FIRV-ZZ, then tests/python/fir+errors run: which tests die per rule branch (the "killers"); (b) ~80 logic mutants (conditions inverted/dropped). docs.title: HEADLINE FINDING: massive duplication across the four Tier-1 verifier files
docs.text: Rule-branch mutation shows almost every Tier-1 branch is killed by exactly 2 tests with identical bodies in different files (e.g. FIRV-T7 StoreField non-class: test_verifier_more::test_t7_store_field_non_class_operand and test_verifier_types::test_t7_store_field_object_non_class_type). Cross-file clusters (same rule branch, near-identical input): - S6 dup type/function/constant, enum no variants, enum has base, unresolved base, cyclic base, generic ref omits args, generic instance wrong arg count: in test_verifier_structure.py (9), test_verifier_more.py (9+3), test_verifier_structural_and_method_call.py (10). Three copies each. - D1/D2/D3 operand resolution: structure(4-5), more(4), structural_and_method_call(2), types_extra(3 "lenient"). - T1/T2 binop/unary: types(7) vs more(6) vs types_extra(4) (e.g. test_t1_arithmetic_result_type_mismatch, test_t1_string_concat_result_not_string, test_t1_logical_operand_not_bool exist with identical names/bodies in types and more). - T5/T6 call/method-call arg-count/arg-mode/result-type/shape: types, more, types_extra, structural_and_method_call, checks. - T7-T12, G1, G3: types vs more (identical names, e.g. test_t10_, test_t11_, test_g3_gen_new_, test_g3_gen_value_). Net: ~85 of ~230 verifier tests could be deleted with zero loss of rule-branch coverage; keep one per branch (preferably in one file, @t.params).

docs.text:
• INCORRECT pipeline_errors::test_for_in_over_array_returning_function_call_hits_known_verifier_bug. Repro in a private copy: fn makeArr() -> int32[] { return [1,2,3]; } for (v: int32 in makeArr()) { } -> "internal compiler error: FIR verification failed (FIRV-T4): Return value type 'int32[3]' does not match declared return type 'int32[]'". Real bug in ast_to_fir (return type not widened) or in verifier _type_assignable not applied to Return. Mutating the T4-return emit (line ~562) kills this test as well as test_t4_return_value_type_mismatch, so fixing the bug will break the test; it asserts the bug.
  • WEAK test_t8_array_copy_non_array_dst_and_src: mutant A (dst check -> if False) 0 failures; mutant B (src check) 0 failures; both emits relabelled individually 0 failures.
  • WEAK test_resolve_method_traverses_base_chain: mutant _resolve_method stops at first class (M11) 0 failures.
  • TRIVIAL test_var_access_declared_type_none_is_skipped: mutant T1 (guard removed) 0 failures. Only T12 NullLiteral emit (also killed by test_t12_null_literal_non_nullable) keeps it green.
  • WEAK errors/test_errors: mutant E1 snippet is not None removed: 0 failures (line=0 short-circuits). Mutant E2 (render fallback) killed by test_render_falls_back... fine.
  • WEAK log_formatter Windows test: mutant L1 (platform.system()=="Windows" -> False): 0 failures.
  • WEAK enum guard tests: mutants T3, T9, O17, O18, O19, O21 survive.
  • TRIVIAL _StateDict test: mutant T5 0 failures; dead class.
  • Mode-count branch in MethodCall: relabel emit line 590: only test_verifier_structural_and_method_call::test_t6_method_call_arg_mode_count_mismatch dies; more::test_t6_method_call_arg_modes_count_mismatch does not (it also violates the arg-count branch) -> WEAK/REDUNDANT.
  • Corrupt IR cleanliness: many tests leave callee FIRFunctions without any block (e.g. test_t5_call_arg_modes_count_mismatch, structural callee in types.py), so FIRV-S1 also fires; and several leave Point allocations with wrong arg counts (e.g. types::test_t7_load_field_unknown_field also violates T9). The expected rule is still emitted by exactly one branch so they do not pass for the wrong reason, but they are not "exactly one violation"; _expect_rule only checks rule in rules, never exclusivity, so a spurious extra violation never fails any test. No valid-twin exists for most rules (valid twins exist for T8 alloc/copy, T5 array size/nullable, L2 nullable, G4, E1-rhs, clean modules).
  • test_verifier_ownership::test_o4_* / o7 use callee FIRFunctions without blocks (S1 on callee) and p passed as own while also needing Return; fine because Tier 2 only runs on clean functions.

docs.title: Compiler bugs discovered (all reproduced in a private copy, python firescript/main.py X.fire --platform windows --arch x86_64)
docs.text:
1. ICE FIRV-T4 for unsized array return: fn makeArr() -> int32[] { return [1, 2, 3]; } (called in for-in or anywhere) -> FIRV-T4 "Return value type 'int32[3]' does not match declared return type 'int32[]'". Pinned by a passing test (above); no known_issues .fire test exists.
  2. import @firescript/std.io.println; const B: bool = true; -> "Code generation failed: could not convert string to float: 'true'" (flir_to_asm._emit_globals "e" in literal check).
  3. import @firescript/std.io.println; const C: char = 'Z'; -> "Code generation failed: invalid literal for int() with base 10: \"'Z'\"" (_normalize_literal_text lacks CHAR_LITERAL; the raw quoted text reaches codegen).
  4. import @firescript/std.io.println; const S: string = "hi"; -> ICE FLIRV-A3 "free/destroy argument is not a heap-allocation base pointer (gload)" (preprocessor inserts drop() of a global const string). (Without the import line, const C: char fails to parse: char type is accepted only after an import; not itself judged a bug here.) Bugs 2-4 are described in test_const_non_numeric_literal_initializers_reach_fir's docstring but tests/sources/known_issues/ has no run-kind file for any of them (only tests/sources/invalid/known_issues/*); CLAUDE.md's convention would have them as failing known-issue tests.
  5. Stale docs in test: int32 y = x++ + 1; now yields parse errors, not an ICE.

docs.title: Detailed evidence (mutations in private copy; each run = whole tests/python/flir, 343 tests)
docs.text:
• E1 Drop S3 offset + fsize > struct.size check (verifier.py if False:): 1 failure = structure::test_s3_rejects_field_exceeding_struct_size. extra::test_s3_field_exceeds_struct_size still passes because it sets struct.size = 6 with align 4, which trips the separate "size not multiple of align" S3 check (its comment "shrink to isolate" is wrong). WEAK.
  • E2 Drop if inst.from_type.kind not in scalar_kinds (cvt from_type not scalar): 0 failures. types and extra "cvt_from_type_not_scalar" both build Cvt(ptr value, from_type=struct Point) which already violates "from_type equals operand's actual type" (T2), so both pass for the wrong reason. The rule is effectively untested.
  • E3 Drop M2 alignment emit: only checks::test_m2_store_misaligned_offset_is_reported fails; types::test_m2_load_misaligned_offset passes (it asserts M1; its offset 5 isn't a field).
  • E4 Drop the empty-block S1 emit: 0 failures; extra::test_s1_empty_block still passes via the other (unreachable) block.
  • E5 Heap meet keeps tokens missing from a predecessor (pass instead of del): 0 failures. E5b Treat any call result as a fresh token (drop kind != "ptr" guard): 0 failures. E5c Rename A2 emit to a bogus id: 5 failures but loops::test_a2_use_after_free_across_back_edge_is_reported is NOT among them (A1 satisfies it).
  • E6 Subnormal rounding. Mutation: replace sig = min(sig, (1<<112)-1) by carrying into the min normal (what IEEE and the independent oracle tests/support/float128_oracle.py do): the only failing test is test_subnormal_rounding_clamps_at_max_subnormal_significand. Direct check for that text "3.3621...e-4932": lowering returns (0xffffffffffffffff, 0xffffffffffff) (largest subnormal), oracle returns (0x0, 0x1000000000000) (smallest normal); frac*2^16494 = 2^112 - 0.4 so correct rounding is up to 2^112 = min normal. => compiler bug B1; the test pins the wrong answer and its comment rationalizes it. Also verified: both "overflow after rounding" tests (f128_decimal ...overflows_to_infinity and _more ...overflows_to_infinity) reach the same branch (inputs are 0.6 ulp and exactly 0.5 ulp above max finite; both match the oracle); f128_decimal's comment calls its input "just below the largest finite" which is wrong (it is above). Mutations show the three float128 files overlap: round-half-even tie -> always-up fails 4 tests across all three files; EXP_BIAS off by one fails 6 tests across 3 files; dropping the NaN sign bit fails 2 (one each in decimal and _more).
  • E7 Loop-header TOP sentinel removed (live = states): 6 failures, all in loops file (a4 pre-loop, a1 pre-loop, a2, nested x2, while). None of hchecks' loop tests nor any valid-twin loop test fails.
  • E8 Tier-1 gate removed (if function.blocks:): fails checks::test_tier2_is_skipped_for_function_with_tier1_violation only (A4 cascade appears).
  • E9 instruction_dominates < -> <=: only edges::test_instruction_dominates_same_block_orders_by_index_strictly fails (no verifier test depends on same-index; fine).
  • Verified valid: heap A5 positive/negative cases, test_verifier_checks assertions, M12 (tag overlap) caught by 2 tests, M11 (S2 struct-field) caught by extra only (it errors with KeyError when check removed; structure's pseudo-test cannot).

docs.title: Compiler bugs discovered
docs.text:
• B1 (lowering.py _decimal_to_f128_bits, subnormal branch, ~line 126): a float128 literal in the subnormal range whose rounded significand reaches 2^112 is clamped to the largest subnormal (0x...ffff) instead of rounding up to the smallest normal (hi=0x0001000000000000, lo=0). 1 ulp error. Repro (no .fire needed): from flir.lowering import _decimal_to_f128_bits as d; d("3.36210314311209350626267781732175234359107456732546680313127e-4932") -> (0xffffffffffffffff, 0xffffffffffff); oracle: (0, 0x1000000000000). Extremely obscure literal; fix is if sig >= 1<<112: return (0, sign<<63 | 1<<48) which makes only the pinning test fail.
  • B2 (flir/lowering.py:1023 lower_binary): float128 ** float128 crashes the compiler with an uncaught Python traceback flir.lowering.LoweringError: unsupported float128 operator ** instead of a user diagnostic. Repro (private copy): file with import @firescript/std.io.println; a: float128 = 2.0f128; b: float128 = 3.0f128; c: float128 = a ** b; println(c); python firescript/main.py x.fire --platform windows --arch x86_64 -o x.exe. No tests/sources known_issues entry exists for it (only this unit test's comment mentions it).

docs.title: Key meta-findings
docs.text:
• Differential as oracle in test_asm_encoding.py IS effective today: I ran all 96 CASES through our assembler vs the host GNU as (ELF path): 96 matched, 0 None (as rejected), 0 empty (oracle extraction failed), 0 mismatches. If extraction broke it would mismatch (ours non-empty), not silently pass. Weaknesses: (a) silent downgrade to len(ours)>0 when as is absent or rejects a line (violates the project's no-silent-weakening spirit; should fail/ERROR when as missing on a host that claims to run it, and always assert len(ours)>0); (b) CASES omits call, jmp, jb, jae, je, jne, jnz, jz, js, mul, shr (all supported by the assembler) because no label forms are used. Mutation: changing _JCC["jb"] 0x82->0x83 survived ALL 211 backend python tests AND the e2e conversions tests (jb only used in fs_rt_mem_copy overlap path). Dropping 'dil' from the setcc REX-force set (4,5,6,7)->(4,5,6) also survived.
  • The float128/ tests test the Python ORACLE (tests/support/float128_oracle.py, a test helper), not the compiler's soft-float runtime (std/internal/float128.fire). The runtime is covered only by 4 .fire files (~47 println total). The docs claim bit-exact fuzz validation vs the oracle but nothing like that is committed; oracle.vectors() is never replayed against the runtime.
  • The oracle itself is CORRECT: I diffed it against glibc libquadmath (__float128, independent implementation) on 32,000 random add/sub/mul/div/lt/le/eq/to_f64 ops over edge-biased bit patterns (subnormal, inf/nan, near-1 exponents) = 0 mismatches; format_f/format_g on 6,030 values = 0 mismatches vs quadmath_snprintf("%.6Qf"/"%Qg"); parse vs Fraction/Decimal rounding on 11 strings incl. 1e4000/1e-5000/4.9e-4951 = 0 mismatches; test_oracle_units' constants all match. So no INCORRECT float128 test. But the units suite is too weak to protect the oracle: mutating _rne tie-to-even (never round-up on odd lsb) and mutating _round_digits tie-to-even (prev % 2 == 1 -> == 0) each survive 14/14.
  • CLI tests share REPO_ROOT/build/ with each other (test_check::test_check_valid_file removes then asserts absence of build/functions.exe while test_default_target_compiles and the test_output tests compile functions.fire from the same cwd). Latent flake under --jobs>1; I could not reproduce in 8 parallel runs (private copy).
  • Large intra-slice duplication: test_assembler_unit.py duplicates test_asm_encoding.py almost completely (33 of 39), test_pe_writer_more.py duplicates test_pe_writer.py (4 of 4), flir_to_asm_coverage duplicates flir_to_asm_errors (4), cli/test_targets.py duplicates test_targets_resolution.py (2), several test_check/test_main_internals CLI tests duplicate stronger test_main_arg_errors tests.

docs.title: Compiler bugs / questionable behaviours discovered
docs.text:
1. python firescript/main.py --dir <dir> exits 0 even when every file in the dir failed to compile (main.py ~L615-636 only logs "N successful, M failed"; no sys.exit(1)). Repro: dir containing bad.fire with x: int32 = ; -> exit=0. Two tests pin this (test_dir_partial_failure, test_dir_with_unsupported_target_counts_failures). Per project rule do not edit the tests to hide; decide intended behavior and fix both.
  2. lint_text("import definitely_missing_module_xyz.helper;\nx: int32 = helper(1);\n") returns [] (no diagnostic) because resolve_imports exception is swallowed (except Exception: return errors). The LSP therefore shows nothing for an unresolved import while the CLI reports "Import resolution failed". Likely a bug (or at least untested; test only asserts isinstance list).
  3. Stale docs in test comments: runtime_state_get/set "segfaults" (false), u64<->float "fails to assemble" (fixed in 913dd4c).
  4. Assembler cannot encode add qword ptr [mem], reg (valid x86) - closed-grammar limitation pinned as an error; fine if the backend never emits it.

docs.title: S1 audit: tests/sources/{classes,memory,nullable,special_types}
docs.text:
Scope: 49 standalone tests (+2 helpers: classes_cross_module_helper.fire, classes_widget_helper.fire; both fine, used by their tests). Verification: every test was compiled and run privately (wine, windows/x86_64); ALL 49 outputs match their EXPECT blocks exactly. Expected values were also derived by hand (float128 values, truncation, nullable logic, ownership semantics). No EXPECT block is wrong. The problems are weakness / redundancy / misleading headers, plus 2 real compiler bugs found while probing (section at the end).

Key structural facts that drive many verdicts (verified): (a) Runtime free is registry-based (firescript/std/internal/alloc.fire fs_rt_free): double-free, and free of string literals, are SILENTLY IGNORED. So "no double free" / "no leak" claims in headers cannot be observed through program output. Only use-after-free via block reuse/corruption, or the FIR/FLIR snapshots, can detect drop bugs. (b) Fixed-size array .length() is constant-folded to a literal in FIR (checked with --emit-fir on memory_branching), so printing it observes nothing about runtime state. (c) msg: string = "iter" is a string literal => drop is a no-op at runtime.

docs.text: Header: "p is never used again; ownership lowering inserts a Drop for it at the end of the function's scope" directly contradicts the first half of the same comment ("no DropInst is ever emitted for p"). --emit-fir of the function shows only alloc/local/loadfield/binop/ret, no drop. The test is titled "regression coverage ... going out of scope" but there is no scope-exit action to cover; the claimed dead-code observation about lowering.py ~1648 is also stale (the is_copyable_class_str uses are now at lines 578/1276/1335/1787). Replace with either deletion, or fix the header to say "copyable class local in a function: no drop emitted, value usable", and consider //@ snapshot: fir so the absence of a drop is actually asserted.

docs.text: println(b.length()) on a fixed-size array literal is folded to const.int32 1 in FIR (verified L2 of memory_branching.fir). Output is a constant independent of runtime heap state; the only things tested are "compiles" and "does not crash". Registry-based free ignores double free. Suggested replacement: one test with //@ snapshot: fir covering block exit, if/else exit and early return together (drops appear in the dump), or a class whose fields are read after unrelated allocation to expose premature free.

docs.title: float128_ops (WEAK) with replacement
docs.text: Every assertion uses 6-digit %f output and exactly representable operands. A float128 implemented as float64 would pass. Verified the runtime is actually correct for these discriminating probes (outputs in parentheses), so they can be added as comparisons (not printing): 1.0f128 + 1.0e-30f128 > 1.0f128 (true; float64 gives false) 1.0f128 + 1.0e-33f128 > 1.0f128 (true) 1.0f128 + 1.0e-35f128 > 1.0f128 (false: below half-ulp, round-to-nearest-even) (1.0f128 + 1.0e-34f128) - 1.0f128 == 0.0f128 (false: rounds up to 1+ulp) zero/zero: nan == nan false, nan != nan true; 1/0 > 1.0e4000f128 true; -zero == zero true 7.5f128 as int64 = 7, -7.5f128 as int64 = -7 (truncation toward zero) These are documented guarantees (type_system.md: correctly rounded, subnormals, signed zero, inf, NaN) with no end-to-end test.

docs.title: Compiler bugs discovered (verified with the current main)
docs.text:
Bug 1: string? parameters (plain functions and ctors/methods) reject null and any string?-typed value with an internal compiler error. Passing a non-null literal works (that is all the existing tests do). int32? parameters work fine (verified), so it is specific to pointer-shaped nullables; the parameter signature keeps string instead of string? at the FIR verifier. Repro A (minimal): import @firescript/std.io.println; fn f(s: string?) -> void { println("in f"); } f(null); -> "FIR verification failed (FIRV-T5): Call argument 0 ('s') has type 'string?', expected 'string'" Repro B: x: string? = "b"; f(x); -> same FIRV-T5. Repro C: class Config{host:string; port:string?; fn Config(&mut this, host:string, port:string?){...}} p: string? = null; new Config("h", p); -> FIRV-T5 ('port'); and a method greet(&this, name: string?) called with null -> FIRV-T6. Docs changelog line 58-59 describe fixing this only for nullable scalars.

Bug 2: function declared -> string? that returns a string literal fails FIR verification. Repro: fn f(b: bool) -> string? { if (b) { return "yes"; } return null; } x: string? = f(true); -> "FIRV-T4 in f/...: Return value type 'string' does not match declared return type 'string?'" (class-typed nullable locals q: P? = null; q = P(3); work fine.)

Neither has a test in tests/sources (not under known_issues either); nullable/ has no string?/class? param or return coverage. Per CLAUDE.md these belong in tests/sources/known_issues/ with header comments.

Minor doc/behaviour mismatches pinned by tests (owner decision, not bugs per se): receiver-less instance methods using this (classes_static_methods twice, memory_implicit_receiver_borrow describe), owned this ctor receiver (classes_owned_this_constructor) vs memory_management.md saying consuming this is PLANNED, ctor with &this receiver (classes_constructor_owned_borrowed_param) vs docs saying ctors take &mut this.

Not verified: that memory_constructor_move / memory_implicit_receiver_borrow would fail on a revert of their fixes (relied on reasoning about Windows heap corruption of freed blocks rather than re-introducing the bugs; I may not modify the repo); the "no other test covers X" claims are based on grep of tests/sources and tests/python filenames/contents, not exhaustive semantic analysis.

docs.title: 1. & "intersection" constraints (INCORRECT x3)
docs.text:
• docs/reference/type_system.md: interface constraints and "Multiple Constraints" (Comparable & (int32|float64)) are marked [PLANNED]; Comparable is not defined anywhere (grep: only mentioned in docs and as a hard-coded allow-list string in firescript/parser/type_system.py:842).
  • firescript/parser/declarations.py:82-86 handles AMPERSAND by appending a literal "&" part and joining with " | ". Probe (s2work/t/b.fire): fn identity<T: int32 & Nonexistent> rejects float64 with message "does not satisfy constraint 'int32 | & | Nonexistent'" -- i.e. the constraint is a union of {int32, "&", Nonexistent}. Probe c.fire: constraint Combo = int32 & float64; identity(5.5f64) is accepted for float64 as well as int32 -- so & currently behaves as union, not intersection.
  • Correct behavior under real intersection semantics: int32 & float64 admits no type (identity(5i32) should be an error); int32 & Comparable with undefined Comparable should be an unknown-type error until interfaces exist. The tests therefore pin an accidental parse artifact of a PLANNED feature, with no [PLANNED] note.
  • Suggested replacement: delete all three; if intersection syntax should be tracked, add a tests/sources/invalid/known_issues/ file expecting an error for T: int32 & float64/unknown interface. Also manifest line 634 should be dropped.

docs.title: 2. scope_stray_token_recovery.fire (INCORRECT)
docs.text:
• Source has a lone ] inside a function body. It compiles with exit 0, no warning, and prints 5. Probe a.fire: a stray ) in a fn body and a stray ] at top level are also silently skipped. In contrast tests/sources/invalid/syntax/syntax_errors.fire expects FS-PARSE-0010/0012 for stray @ # $. The ] is dropped in parse_scope's "no progress -> force advance" guard (firescript/parser/statements.py:664-668), because _parse_statement returns None without reporting an error.
  • Correct behavior: a syntax error (FS-PARSE-*). The test validates "recovery" by asserting the invalid program is valid. Replace with a tests/sources/invalid/syntax test (or known_issues/ version) //~ ERROR FS-PARSE-xxxx on the ]. Unlike control_flow/empty_statements.fire (legit ;), this is not valid input.

docs.title: 3. copyable generic class with a string (soft INCORRECT)
docs.text:
• docs/reference/classes.md "Copyable Classes": all fields must be Copyable. generics_class_basic.fire p2 (Pair<int32,string>) and generics_class_inferred_construct.fire (Pair<int32,string>) violate it. The compiler does not enforce the rule at all (probe q.fire: non-generic copyable class S { name: string } also compiles silently), and p.fire shows a bit-copy p3 = p2 of such a value compiles and runs (potential double-free of the string, not observed here).
  • The docs' own example uses the same copyable class Pair<T,U>, so this is partly a docs/compiler gap; but tests should not rely on it. Suggested: use class Pair<T,U> (owned) for the string instantiations, keep copyable for int/int; add an invalid test for copyable-with-owned-field.

docs.title: 4. generators_frame_zero_init_types.fire (WEAK + stale)
docs.text:
• Header says the test checks locals are zero-initialised in __init independent of their source initialiser, but every local (flag, big, v, i) has an explicit initialiser and is read only after assignment, so the zero-init is unobservable: the test would pass if _zero_value returned garbage. It only proves bool/float128/copyable-struct locals survive across yields.
  • Header also says pointer-kind generator locals (string/array/class) crash with FLIRV-T1. That is no longer true: probe g2/g3.fire (string, int32[2], class locals in a generator) compile and print correctly. So the "intentionally avoids" rationale is stale and the test now omits the most valuable cases. Suggested: add string/array/class locals (g3.fire passes), and to observe zero-init, yield before a local's first assignment ... or just retitle as "mixed-type generator locals". Also update the stale header.

docs.title: 5. scoping_variable_declaration_order.fire (header/claim mismatch)
docs.text: • Comment (and TEST_MANIFEST line 555) says "same variable name across different sibling scopes are separate variables", but the names are value2, value3, value4 -- all distinct, nothing is reused. docs/reference/scoping.md section 5 says reusing a name across sibling scopes is OK. Probe e.fire (v declared in a bare block, an if body and a for body) works and prints 1,2,3. Replace the distinct names with v so the test checks what it claims (also before/after = before+1 half is trivial).

docs.title: 6. functions_many_params.fire (WEAK)
docs.text: • All checks are commutative sums (a+b+c+d+e; p.x+p.y), so a swapped/misplaced stack argument (the exact class of bug a >4-arg ABI test must catch) still gives 15 / 17.5 / 40. Also only 5 params; no interleaved int/float mix (Win64 shares slots) and no 2nd struct. Probe m.fire with positional weights (a+10b+100c+...) over 7 int params, 7 mixed int/float32-64 params, and 2 struct params passes (7654321 each), so the stronger test is safe to adopt.

docs.title: 7. operator_precedence.fire (minor WEAK, comment errors)
docs.text: • 10 % 3 + 1: comment says wrong precedence would give 1; it gives 10%(3+1)=2, the same as correct (2): does not discriminate. r7 = false && false || false is false under any grouping: non-discriminating. The comment on 4 / 2 ** 2 ("not 1 (same here...)") is wrong: correct is 1, wrong grouping (4/2)**2 = 4, so it does discriminate. All other lines verified discriminating and EXPECT correct (14,4,8,2,18,1,2,3,9,tftt..: true,false,true,true,true,true,false,false,false,20,14,64). No unary-vs-** (-2 ** 2), ! or as precedence cases; ** associativity lives in operators_regression_power_assign.fire.

docs.title: 8. fall-off-the-end returns (soft INCORRECT)
docs.text:
• No doc specifies it (grep docs/reference: none). The three tests assert implicit zero for bool/int32/float64/float128. Probe h2.fire: the same shape with a string return ICEs (FIRV-T4), so behavior is inconsistent by type -- this is an accident of ast_to_fir._synthesize_zero, not a design. The header of functions_missing_return_fallthrough.fire itself says "no missing return diagnostic exists" and the repo has just added known_issues for other missing diagnostics. Correct long-term behavior is a missing-return diagnostic; these tests will then break. Consolidate into one explicitly-labelled "current behavior" test or move to known_issues with the expected diagnostic.
  • Also stale: functions_return_types.fire says char cannot be a return type and is untestable. Probe h1.fire: fn f(n) -> char { if (n>1) { return 'a'; } } compiles; f(2)='a', f(0) prints a NUL char.

docs.title: 9. functions_explicit_owned_param.fire (WEAK)
docs.text: • Duplicate of memory/memory_owned_function_param.fire; additionally asserts nothing about ownership (no use-after-move diagnostic, no drop observation). The doc rule ("owned params move into the function; argument invalid after the call") is what should be tested, in invalid/borrow.

docs.title: Compiler bugs discovered
docs.text:
1. Nested generator ICE (header of generators_advanced.fire; no known_issues test exists): fn inner() -> generator<int32> { yield 1; yield 2; } fn outer() -> generator<int32> { for (x: int32 in inner()) { yield x * 10; } } for (v: int32 in outer()) { println(v); } -> "FLIR verification failed (FLIRV-T5)" internal compiler error (reproduced, g1.fire). Should get a known_issues test.
  2. Non-scalar fall-off-the-end return ICE: fn s(n: int32) -> string { if (n > 1) { return "x"; } } -> FIRV-T4 internal compiler error (h2.fire). Should be a clean missing-return diagnostic (no such known_issues file exists; return_missing_value.fire covers only bare return;).
  3. Function reading a global is an ICE although docs say it works: docs/reference/scoping.md ("User-defined functions also have access to global variables", section 6 example) is marked [IMPLEMENTED], but g: int32 = 10; fn f() -> int32 { return g + 1; } println(f()); -> "FIR verification failed (FIRV-L1)" internal error (d.fire). The scoping_function.fire header ("can't access outer scope variables in the current implementation") knows about the limitation but nothing tracks it; docs and compiler disagree and should not both stand. Needs either a clean diagnostic or implementation, plus a known_issues test.
  4. Stray ] / ) tokens inside a scope are silently dropped with exit 0 (parser/statements.py:664-668; probes a.fire). Missing syntax diagnostic.
  5. & in generic constraints is parsed into a "|"-joined list containing "&" (declarations.py:82-86), so it silently means union; and the constraint-check at type_system.py:842 exempts any constraint string equal to Numeric/Comparable/... from checking.
  6. Copyable-class field rule (all fields Copyable) is not enforced (q.fire).
  7. % is accepted on any same-type type parameter (type_system.py:625) even when the constraint allows floats (generic_function_same_type_param_modulo.fire's Numeric = int32 | float32), whereas the concrete-type path requires integers (docs: integer operands). Not exercised by a test; noted only.
  8. (not a bug) docs/reference has no description of fn main() entry-point semantics or the "top-level ignored" warning that function_main_ignores_top_level.fire pins.

docs.title: Could not verify
docs.text:
• Snapshot (.fir/.flir) content correctness was not reviewed in depth (only existence and that FIR is not constant-folded for operator_precedence).
  • float128 as string formatting ("0.000000"/"2.500000") assumed consistent with special_types tests (not independently derived).
  • Whether any python test under tests/python independently covers the nested-generator or & constraint cases (grep for "generator"/"intersection" found only parser dead-guard tests, none asserting those behaviors).

docs.title: S3 audit: types / conversions / operators / edge_cases / identifiers / io  (53 files)
docs.text: Method: every file compiled + run in a private temp dir (wine) with my own runner; all 53 outputs MATCH their EXPECT blocks, so no test is stale. Numerics re-derived with a Python oracle (two's-complement wrap, struct float32 rounding, printf %f for float64). All EXPECT values are arithmetically right under the compiler's actual semantics; the INCORRECT verdicts below are about pinning behavior that contradicts the docs or is undefined/undocumented. Docs facts used: type_system.md L141-153 and error_handling.md L31-38 say fixed-width int overflow TRAPS at runtime (compile error if constant-detectable). Float printing is printf "%f" (6 digits; stated in special_types/float128_ops.fire). Harness normalisation (tests/harness/expectations.py:20) rstrips every line and strips trailing blank lines.

docs.title: #1 INCORRECT: wraparound pinned where docs mandate a trap
docs.text: types_int8.fire, types_uint8.fire, edge_cases_overflow_underflow.fire expect 127i8 + 1i8 = -128, -128i8 - 1i8 = 127, 255u8 + 1u8 = 0. docs/reference/type_system.md L141-153 and error_handling.md L31-38: "arithmetic ... that exceeds the representable range will throw an error at runtime ... constant expressions are compile-time errors". The compiler wraps silently (also int32: 2147483647 + 1 -> -2147483648, 2 ** 31 -> -2147483648, uint8 0-1 -> 255; verified by probe). Either the compiler is wrong (and these must move to tests/sources/known_issues/ or become an expected-trap test), or the docs are stale; in both cases blessing wrap silently is wrong. Owner decision needed; stress_integer_overflow.fire (performance/, out of my slice) pins the same wrap. Suggested: delete the overflow lines from the three files; add one test that states the decided semantics (trap test, or // note + wrap test if docs get changed).

docs.text: toChar("65") expects 6; toChar(66) (other file) expects B. TEST_MANIFEST documents "toChar on a string takes its first character's code point". No reference doc defines these builtins; parser/type_system.py L873 still special-cases them. Not wrong per se but unspecified and self-inconsistent; recommend confirming the builtins are supported, otherwise mark known-legacy. If kept, drop the toChar("65") line.

docs.text: f1 as int8 (200.9) -> -56, as int16 -> 200: out-of-range float->narrow-int is UB in C, docs only say "may lose precision or truncate". Probe results (all pinned nowhere): NaN as int32 = 0, inf as int32 = 0, inf as int64 = -9223372036854775808, 300.5 as uint8 = 44, -1.5 as uint8 = 255, -1.0 as uint64 = 18446744073709551615, 2147483648.0 as int32 = -2147483648, 1e10 as int32 = 1410065408. Keep only in-range cases (the uint64 >2^63 lines are good and verified: float32(1.8e19) = 18000000404716257280 exact), or document the semantics first.

docs.title: #4 conversions_regression_uint64_to_float.fire (WEAK + real bug)
docs.text: Header says the odd value (2^63+1) checks "the halving step must keep the sticky bit". 2^63+1 rounds to 2^63 with or without a sticky bit, so the case cannot fail. A value that does need it: 9223372036854776833u64 (= 2^63+1025). Correct float64: 9223372036854777856.000000 (python float(2**63+1025)). Compiler prints 9223372036854775808.000000: WRONG (see bugs). Replacement lines: println(9223372036854776833u64 as float64); expect 9223372036854777856.000000 (will fail until fixed => known_issues convention or fix compiler first).

docs.title: #5 conversions_float_precision.fire
docs.text: Header: "Float64 to float32 (precision loss)". Output shows no loss: 3.141593 / 3.141593 (6-digit %f). Test cannot detect a no-op cast. Replacement: println((precise as float32) as float64 == precise) expect false; println((0.1f as float64) == 0.1) expect false (I verified the latter is false today), println((16777217.0 as float32) as float64) expect 16777216.000000.

docs.title: #6 float ** fractional exponent (see bugs); operators_arithmetic.fire should add println(2.0 ** 0.5) -> 1.414214, 9.0 ** 0.5 -> 3.000000.
WEAK summary of printing
docs.text: Every float assertion goes through %f (6 decimals) so float32 vs float64 storage, subnormals, rounding mode and NaN/inf formatting (inf/-inf/nan do print as inf, -inf, nan; -0.0 prints -0.000000) are essentially untested in this slice; no test in the slice covers NaN, inf, float overflow (3.4e38f32*10 -> inf works), or the documented type_system.md NaN/Infinity examples.

docs.title: Compiler bugs discovered (all reproduced in private dir)
docs.text:
1. NaN comparisons are wrong (IEEE says all false except !=): z: float64 = 0.0; n: float64 = z / z; println(n == n) -> true (expected false) println(n == 1.0) -> true (false); n < 1.0 -> true (false); n <= 1.0 -> true (false); n > 1.0, n >= 1.0 false (ok) same for float32. Docs: "Floating point operations follow IEEE 754 semantics". Looks like ucomisd with unordered (ZF=PF=CF=1) not checked for PF.
  2. Float ** ignores fractional exponent: println(2.0 ** 0.5) -> 1.000000 (1.414214); 9.0 ** 0.5 -> 1.000000 (3); 2.0 ** 1.5 -> 2.000000 (2.828427); 10.0 ** 2.5 -> 100.000000 (316.227766). Integer exponents are fine. Exponent is truncated.
  3. uint64 -> float64 loses the sticky bit: println(9223372036854776833u64 as float64) -> 9223372036854775808.000000, correct 9223372036854777856.000000. (2^63+1025; not rounded up; values < 2^63 and exact halves are fine.)
  4. Integer overflow wraps instead of trapping (docs contradiction, see #1).
  5. 2 ** -1 (int) prints 1 (undocumented; should likely be error or 0); int 5 / z with z == 0 raises a raw hardware divide-by-zero (wine: "Unhandled division by zero"), not the documented firescript runtime error. Not covered by any test in my slice.
  6. Float->int casts of out-of-range/NaN/inf values are silent and inconsistent between widths (see #3 list) - spec gap more than bug.

Could not verify: native Windows behavior (only wine); the harness's own run of these tests (not run per instructions; my private runner reproduced all 53 EXPECT blocks); the redundancy claims for edge_cases_* vs scoping/functions/arrays tests rest on grep + reading, not on mutation testing.

docs.title: Evidence for INCORRECT / WEAK findings
docs.text:
E1 arrays/array_tests.fire INCORRECT. println(numbers) (numbers: int32[] = [10,20,30,40,50]) and println(names) are expected to print [...]. That literal comes from flir/lowering.py::_array_to_string fallback ConstStr("[...]") used when the array length is unknown. Probe: a: int32[]=[10,20,30]; println(a) -> [...]; b: int32[3]=[1,2,3]; println(b) -> [...] (even statically sized!), but println(b as string) -> [1, 2, 3] and array_to_string.fire expects [1, 2, 3] for the same data. So println(array) silently degrades to a placeholder while as string works: the EXPECT block blessed a compiler inconsistency/placeholder. Suggest: fix compiler or delete the println(array) lines; this test is the only place [...] appears in tests/. The rest of the file is redundant.

E2 control_flow_braceless_if_at_eof.fire INCORRECT (pins likely-bug). The source ends with if (b) and no body and compiles successfully (probe: exit 0) and runs. A dangling if with no statement is malformed; the test was written to cover a parser fallback branch (_parse_braceless_body returning None at EOF) and blesses it as valid. Suggest: make the parser emit a diagnostic and move this to tests/sources/invalid/ (compile-fail with //~ ERROR), or at minimum state in the header that it is a pinned leniency. Mark with owner decision.

E3 Trailing-blank-line blindness. strings_index_of_substring: println(s.substring(10,2)) prints "" as the final line; strings_upper_lower: last two printlns print "" . normalize_output() strips them so e.g. a regression that printed "x" is caught but one that printed " " or nothing is not, and an off-by-one that returns the empty string vs nothing cannot be distinguished. Fix: wrap in markers (println("[" + s.substring(10,2) + "]") -> []) or reorder so the empty case is not last. Also add a one-line header note that substring clamps out-of-range bounds (negative start -> 0, end>len -> len, start>end -> "") since this is pinned but undocumented (only the changelog mentions the methods).

E4 strings_comparison WEAK. Only literal-vs-literal equal ("apple"=="apple", which may be interned/pointer-equal), and one unequal same-length-class case. Missing: different lengths with common prefix ("app" vs "apple"), equal-length-different-content ("abc" vs "abd"), empty string, and equal strings built at runtime ("ap"+"ple" vs "apple") which would catch a pointer-compare regression. I probed all of these: they currently work (false,true,false,true,true,true,false), so the replacement is just those lines.

E5 strings_unicode WEAK. Only round-trips bytes through println. Probe: "café".length() == 5 (byte count, not 4 chars), so length/indexOf/for-in semantics on non-ASCII are byte-based and undocumented; test pins none of it (good: not wrongly pinned, but also would not catch a regression in length/slicing on multibyte input). Suggest adding .length() expectation only once the owner decides the intended semantics.

E6 arrays_typed WEAK. int8 array reads only [0] and length; int64 reads only [1]; f64 only [1]; bool [0],[1]. A wrong element stride for int8/int16/uint8 (1-byte elements) would be invisible at index 0. Read the last element of each typed array (and at least 3 elements of the int8 one); other widths (uint8/16/32/64, int16, char) absent.

E7 for_in_and_match_temporaries WEAK/misfiled. Bundles match-on-call-result and sized-array-declaration paths (not control flow). uninitialized: int32[4] reads only [0]: zero-initialization of a sized array is only asserted for one element of one array in the whole suite (array_to_string's int32[0] has no elements); a fresh stack frame may already be zero there. Suggest reading all 4 elements, and after dirtying the stack with a prior function call. Also relocate the match/array-decl parts to match/ and arrays/.

stress_*: manifest (tests/TEST_MANIFEST.md lines 659-665) describes these as "stress", "heavy", "repeated" tests; none loops more than 10 times or allocates more than a few objects. There is NO real performance/stress test in the directory. Runtimes are all <2 s including wine start-up, so nothing is slow; nothing stresses either. Suggested real stress tests: recursion depth ~1e5 (stack limit behavior), a 1e6-iteration loop with string concatenation/drop (leak/allocator), a large (e.g. 1e5-element) array fill/sum.

docs.title: Compiler bugs / doc mismatches discovered (minimal repros; all verified by me under wine)
docs.text:
B1 println(array) prints "[...]" (see E1): a: int32[3] = [1,2,3]; println(a); // prints [...] ; println(a as string) prints [1, 2, 3]

B2 Out-of-range array index is unchecked, reads garbage; docs/reference/arrays.md says it "will cause a runtime error": a: int32[] = [1,2,3]; i: int32 = 5; println(a[i]); println("after"); // prints 6029362 then "after", exit 0 No test anywhere pins OOB behavior; stress_array_bounds does not either.

B3 Signed integer overflow wraps silently; docs/reference/error_handling.md says it "traps at runtime rather than silently wrapping": a: int32 = 2147483647; b: int32 = a + 1; println(b); // prints -2147483648, exit 0 (stress_integer_overflow never overflows, so the doc/impl mismatch is not caught. edge_cases/edge_cases_overflow_underflow.fire is labelled "behavior may vary"; outside my slice.)

B4 ICE returning an array literal from an int32[] function (also noted in for_in_and_match_temporaries header, but NOT captured by any known-issue test; note tests/sources/known_issues/ does not exist, only invalid/known_issues/): fn mk() -> int32[] { return [1,2,3]; } x: int32[] = mk(); println(x.length()); -> FIR verifier dump (FIRV-T4 'int32[3]' vs declared 'int32[]'), no binary. (functions_array_return.fire only returns a param.)

B5 if (b) with no body at EOF compiles (see E2).

B6 String literal with embedded NUL truncates: r: string = "a\rb\0c"; println(r.length()); -> 3 (expected 5): strings are NUL-terminated C-style; string_escape_edge_cases.fire header claims \0 is handled but no test exercises it. Likely a known limitation; worth a documented note or a test.

docs.text: Method: all 58 standalone tests (helpers excluded) compiled and run under wine from private temp dirs (private root with build/temp and copies of the integration .txt files). ALL 58 PASS against their EXPECT blocks (runner: scratchpad/audit/run_all.py). I re-derived expected output by hand / with python for: hackathon8_mission1 (576 = signed sum, confirmed), hackathon8_mission2 (17 = mode of unsigned magnitudes, 59 vs runner-up 54, robust), run_length_encoding (python itertools.groupby == EXPECT), fcl lexer offsets, math/ranges/split/fs/cli semantics against docs and std sources. No EXPECT block was found to bless a compiler bug. Findings are mostly redundancy, weak assertions and stale header comments.

docs.title: Detailed evidence: WEAK findings (no INCORRECT)
docs.text:
1. Missing is_match semantics pin: documented "without anchors the pattern must match the entire input; ^ and $ control anchoring". No test asserts is_match("^abc","abcd") (engine: false = Python fullmatch) or is_match("abc$","xabc") (engine: false). Only abc$ vs abcx and ^abc vs xabc are tested, which would also pass under "search" semantics for... (they'd fail under search too, so the gap is the prefix/suffix-with-extra-text direction). Suggested: add both lines to std_regex_anchors.fire (expect false, false).
  2. Escapes , , in the pattern (doc "Supported Syntax") are never tested (grep over tests/ finds none). Probe: is_match("a b","a b"), , all true. Suggest a 3-line test.
  3. Mid-pattern ^/$ as literals (documented) untested. Probe: is_match("a^b","a^b") true, is_match("a$b","a$b") true. Python would treat them as anchors (never matches) - intentional deviation, should be pinned.
  4. . matching newline (documented, differs from Python) untested. Probe is_match("a.c","a c") true.
  5. find_at out-of-range / negative / invalid pattern (documented -1) untested: probe find_at("a","a",-1) = -1, find_at("a","a",5) = -1, find_at("(a","a",0) = -1, find_at("a*","a",1) = 0 (empty match at end).
  6. matches() and find_match() aliases untested. Probe: find_match("a+","aaa") true.
  7. $10 in replacement (documented: only $0..$9): probe replace("(a)","a","$10") -> "a0". Untested.
  8. \s with \v : \v/ cannot be written as firescript string escapes (probe: "a\vb" does not match a\sb, so the literal is not a VT), so only is testable by literal; probe is true. Not verified for \v .
  9. find_all free-function with invalid pattern (doc: empty list) only covered through RegexPattern.find_all in regexpattern_search.

docs.title: Compiler/engine differences vs Python re (all low severity; none are test failures)
docs.text:
• Capture of an empty final iteration: (a*)+ on "aab": Python group1 = '' (last iteration empty), engine group1 = "aa" (0:2). Same for (a*)*b on "aab" (Python '', engine "aa"). (a*)* on "b": Python group1 = '' at (0,0), engine reports group 1 as non-participating (-1). Matches docs ("stops as soon as an iteration consumes nothing") so arguably design, but Python/PCRE differ. Repro: find_first("(a*)+","aab",0).group(1). Not pinned by any test (captures_quantified_group does not cover empty last iteration).
  • (a?){3}a on "aa": engine group1 = 1:"" ; Python group1 = '' too (consistent).
  • All other ~45 extra probes (alternation, nested/optional groups, [a-], [-a], [a-c-e], [\]], [\\], (\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?, (a|b)*, ((a)|b)+ stale-group semantics) matched Python. Documented-intentional deviations (not bugs): . matches \n; [] errors; ^/$ mid-pattern literal; (?...), non-greedy, backrefs unsupported.

docs.title: S7 audit: tests/sources/invalid/{classes,borrow,generics}  (72 files, no helpers)
docs.text:
Method: read every file; ran the real compiler (--check --message-format json) on each; wrote /scratchpad/audit/cmp.py to confirm annotations == actual diagnostics (all 72 currently pass, so no stale columns); wrote ~30 scratch programs in /tmp/.../scratchpad/audit/t/ (a1..f4) to separate primary errors from cascades and probe for missed diagnostics. Parser facts used as redundancy evidence: firescript/parser/declarations.py lines 140/188/194 (receiver/param parsing shared by methods AND constructors), 1069 (static ctor), 1086 (')' after params), 1109 ('{' body); expressions.py:247 (single site for "'(' after constructor type").

IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL FACTS * Any parse error stops the pipeline before semantic analysis. So every file that mixes a parse error with semantic mistakes silently hides the semantic ones (see class_errors, generics_errors). * Many tests annotate CASCADE diagnostics (e.g. "Variable 'this' not defined", "Function 'Pair' is not defined", "Variable 'identity' not defined" where the name IS defined). These lock incidental error-recovery behaviour into the test; any parser-recovery improvement breaks them.

docs.title: DETAILED EVIDENCE (INCORRECT / WEAK)
docs.text:
D1 classes/class_errors.fire (INCORRECT) Intended: undefined class, unknown field, field type mismatch, unknown method, duplicate class, duplicate field, class name used as variable, uninitialized instance. Actual annotated diagnostics (10): - l.5 UndefinedClass obj; : old C-style declaration syntax; the two PARSE-0010 "Expected assignment, function call..." are not an undefined-class error. - l.16/22/28/63 p: Point; : declaration without initializer -> PARSE-0010 "Expected '=' in variable declaration" (variables.md: declarations without initializer unsupported). The intended field/method errors are never reached. - l.17/23/29 PARSE-0003 "Variable 'p' not defined": pure cascade of the failed declaration. - l.64 PARSE-0012 "Function 'println' is not defined": println is not imported (incidental), not the intended obj.required problem. - l.38-44 duplicate class, l.47-50 duplicate field, l.54 Point: int32 = 5 : NO diagnostic, because parse errors suppress semantic analysis. In isolation (scratch a4) the compiler ALSO reports nothing for them (compiler bug B1). Fix: delete the file (every legitimate rule is covered elsewhere: unknown field = field_access_errors, unknown method = unknown_instance_method) and add real tests for duplicate class/field once B1 is fixed (known_issues).

D2 generics/generics_errors.fire (INCORRECT + WEAK; 6 annotations) - l.5 T x;: old syntax; PARSE-0010 x2 are not "undefined type parameter". - l.15 x: int32 = identity<string>(42): comment says "expects string but got int" (argument mismatch). The compiler does NOT check the argument (scratch c4/c8: identity<string>(42) and identity<int32>("s") compile clean). The annotated SEM-0002 comes only from declared-type int32 vs result string. Test passes for the wrong reason and would keep passing if the arg check were never written. - l.19-24 add<T: Numeric> with undefined constraint Numeric, then add<string>(..): unannotated, NO diagnostic even in isolation (c5): undefined constraint and violating call both silently accepted (compiler bug B4). - l.29 identity(5); valid program, comment "May require explicit type parameter" is wrong. - l.34 identity<int32,string>(5) SEM-0010 type-arg count: the only correct, unique case (no other file tests generic function type-arg count). Move it to its own file. - l.43-44 box: Box<int32>; no initializer -> PARSE-0010; l.44 PARSE-0003 "box not defined" is a cascade; intended "generic class field type mismatch" untested (and b.value = "s" is undetected anyway, B2).

D3 Malformed nested/unclosed type-argument tests using obsolete name-first syntax (INCORRECT) generic_class_nested_unclosed_type_args.l.14 Pair<p: Pair<int32,int32 int32> = Pair(...), nested_generic_missing_close_errors.l.14 Pair<Pair<int32, int32, p: string;, generic_declaration_errors.l.24/28 Pair<c: Pair<...> = good; These are leftovers from an older Pair<..> name declaration order. Under current name: Type syntax the line is parsed as an expression statement starting with Pair <, so the first annotation is PARSE-0010 "Expected assignment, function call, or method call" @col 1/5 (statement dispatch), not "missing '>'". generic_declaration_errors l.24/28 additionally yield FS-SEM-0002 "Expected Pair, got Pair" / "Expected int32, got Pair" which are nonsense type-mismatch cascades. The properly-formed variants work and give a sane primary error (scratch c1: p: Pair<Pair<int32,int32, int32> = Pair(Pair(1,2),3); -> PARSE-0010 "Expected '>' to close generic type arguments" @35 + cascade PARSE-0012; c2 likewise). Rewrite these three files with the current syntax (and then they collapse into generic_class_unclosed_type_args).

D4 generics/generic_class_field_access_unknown.fire l.18 (INCORRECT: locks compiler bug) b: Box<int32> = new Box<int32>(5); with fn Box(value: T) defined is rejected: "No constructor defined for type 'Box'" (also for copyable class, and with &mut this: b2,b3). Same program with Box<int32>(5) compiles (b1). new Generic<T>(...) is undocumented/untested anywhere valid (grep docs/examples/tests: no hit), so the rejection is a bug or an unimplemented form, not an intentional rule. The test demands it.

D5 borrow/loop_move_errors.fire, for_in_move_errors.fire (WEAK) while(..){ consume(a); } with a declared outside the loop: the second iteration uses the moved value, yet the compiler reports nothing at the call site (scratch a1: while loop, no later use -> zero diagnostics). The tests only demand the use AFTER the loop ("may have been moved on another control-flow path"). Either (a) the in-loop move should be an error and the tests are missing it, or (b) it is intentionally allowed; docs/reference/memory_management.md l.136 only says "Values used across iterations drop after loop", so the intent is unspecified. At minimum a spec decision + test is needed. Same for for-in (for_in_move_errors l.13).

D6 Cascade-locked annotations (WEAK, systemic) FS-PARSE-0003 "Variable 'this' not defined" after a failed method/ctor parameter list: class_constructor_syntax_errors (6), constructor_param_syntax_errors (7), class_def_syntax_errors (1), constructor_amp_not_this, constructor_param_array_unsupported (2), constructor_param_bad_type (2). FS-PARSE-0012 "Function 'Pair' is not defined" etc. after a failed generic declaration: generic_class_type_arg_errors, generic_class_nested_type_arg_errors, generic_class_unclosed_type_args, generic_class_nested_unclosed_type_args. FS-PARSE-0003 "Variable 'identity'/'Box' not defined" where the name IS defined: generic_call_errors (4), generic_func_empty_type_args (1). FS-PARSE-0003 "Variable 'x' not defined" for params after a failed fn header: generic_def_syntax_errors (4). FS-PARSE-0010 "Expected initializer expression" duplicates: new_missing_paren, new_constructor_syntax_errors, new_constructor_empty_type_args, type_member_access_errors. Duplicate diagnostics for one fault: unknown new type reports PARSE-0012 AND SEM-0010 at the same column (class_new_constructor_errors l.19-20, new_constructor_syntax_errors l.14-15, new_unknown_type l.5-7).

====================================================================================================

Generics: wrong number of type args on a generic CLASS (Box<int32,int32> -> no error, B5); wrong argument type for explicit/inferred generic call (B3); conflicting inference (same(1,"a") reports odd "Could not infer" + SEM-0002 "got T"); undefined constraint name (B4); constraint violation on a generic CLASS type arg; unknown generic class/type name in type-arg list; type-param shadowing / duplicate type param names (fn f<T,T>).

docs.title: COMPILER BUGS / ODDITIES DISCOVERED (minimal repros; scratch files in .../scratchpad/audit/t/)
docs.text:
B1 Duplicate class / duplicate field / class name shadowed by variable produce no diagnostic (a4): class A { x: int32; } class A { y: int32; } class B { x: int32; x: int32; } fn f()->void{ A: int32 = 5; } (the second A silently wins: A() later reports "expected 1 args, got 0" referencing the wrong class) B2 Field assignment/return type mismatch not detected (d1/d2): p: Point = Point(1,2); p.x = "string"; // no error fn get(&this)->string{ return this.x; } // x:int32, no error B3 Explicit/inferred generic call argument type not checked (c4, c8): fn identity(v:T)->T{return v;} x: string = identity(42); a: int32 = identity("s"); // no error B4 Undefined constraint name accepted; violation not reported (c5): fn add(a:T,b:T)->T{return a+b;} add("a","b"); B5 Wrong number of type args on generic class accepted (f3): a: Box = Box(1); // no error B6 new GenericClass<int32>(5) rejected with "No constructor defined for type 'Box'" although constructor exists; Box<int32>(5) accepted (b1/b2/b3). Valid program rejected or undocumented form (see D4). B7 Borrow checker holes (e1,e4,f1,d4): storing &text param into this.text; assigning/mutating through &w param (w.text = "z"); calling &mut this method (c.inc()) on a &c param; s = "x" on &s: string -- all accepted although memory_management.md l.59/78 say borrows are read-only and non-retainable. B8 Move inside loop body not diagnosed (a1/D5). B9 Unknown base class class C from Missing and cyclic inheritance accepted (e6). B10 Misleading cascade diagnostics: after a failed generic call/decl the compiler says "Variable 'identity'/'Box'/'Pair' not defined" or "Function 'Pair' is not defined" for names that ARE defined; after failed params this "not defined". B11 class NoCtor{x:int32;}: NoCtor() is accepted (implicit field constructor, "expected 1 args") but new NoCtor(5) -> "No constructor defined" (a6; class_static_method_errors.l.15 relies on Tool() with no ctor being legal). classes.md documents neither implicit constructors nor this asymmetry. B12 Methods without a receiver (fn add(a:int32) using this.value) and receiver-less constructors compile and are treated as instance methods; classes.md says receivers are required and static needs static fn. A large part of the slice (instance_method_, super_call_, constructor_call_, field_access_) is written in this receiver-less style, i.e. relies on undocumented behaviour. (static fn + this does error: b6.) B13 Re-assigning a moved owned variable (x = "again" after consume(x)) is reported as use-after-move at the assignment (f4); spec silent. B14 Unknown declared type reports PARSE-0010 "Expected type" + PARSE-0003 "Variable 'Undefined' not defined" (c7) rather than an undefined-type diagnostic.

NOT VERIFIED: whether B7/B8/B13 are intentional design (docs are ambiguous; memory_management.md marks borrow rules IMPLEMENTED); whether instance-method statement vs initializer contexts take different semantic paths (instance_method_arg_count/type/unknown marked redundant on message equality only); error CODE choice (PARSE-0012 for "Array parameters not supported", SEM-0010 for nearly everything) was not judged against a spec because errors.py has no per-code docs.

docs.title: types/semantic_modulo_mismatch.fire
docs.text: b: int64 = 6; is annotated //~ ERROR FS-SEM-0002 @5. docs/reference/type_system.md:102-111 states "When you assign a literal to a variable with an explicit type, the literal automatically takes on that type" (large: int64 = 9223372036854775807;, small: int8 = 42;). The compiler rejects ALL of these (repro r7.fire: int8, uint16, float32, int64 all Expected X, got int32/float64). Either the docs are wrong or the compiler is; either way this test (and any test in the suite using unsuffixed literals for non-int32 types) encodes the current bug as expected behavior. All valid tests in the suite use suffixes (100i64), hiding the problem. The intended mod-mismatch error (line 6) is correct.

docs.title: Compiler bugs discovered (minimal repros)
docs.text:
1. Unsuffixed literals not inferred to the declared type (docs say they are): b: int64 = 6; -> FS-SEM-0002 Expected int64, got int32; also small: int8 = 42;, medium: uint16 = 30000;, pi: float32 = 3.14; (docs/reference/type_system.md:104-112). Pinned as "expected" by types/semantic_modulo_mismatch.fire:5.
  2. Undefined free-function call in a file that has any import is accepted by --check (check is deferred, never fires): import @firescript/std.io.println; undefinedFunction(1); -> no diagnostic; full compile fails with plain log FIR->FLIR lowering failed: call to unknown function undefinedFunction (no code/location). Without the import it correctly reports FS-PARSE-0012 (statements.py:195-205). Missing from known_issues.
  3. Array literal / element type mismatches not diagnosed by check; full compile gives internal compiler errors: a: int32[3] = [1, "two", 3]; -> FLIRV-T1; n: int32[] = [1,2,3]; n[0] = "string"; -> FIRV-T8; a5: int32[3]=...; a6: int32[5]=...; a5 = a6; -> FIRV-L2.
  4. Array initializer length vs declared size not diagnosed (docs/reference/arrays.md:27 says "Error"): a: int32[5] = [1,2,3]; and b: int32[3] = [1,2,3,4,5]; both compile silently.
  5. match: pattern of a different enum than the scrutinee (s: A; match s { B.P -> {} _ -> {} }) and a non-enum scrutinee (n: int32; match n { _ -> {} }) compile with no diagnostic; value-producing match with arm-type mismatch (Shape.Circle(radius) -> radius, Shape.Point -> "zero" assigned to float64) -> FIR ICE FIRV-L2 instead of a semantic error. (docs have no match-typing rules to cite, but the ICE is a bug regardless.)
  6. Cyclic import detection is dead code; a cycle produces Variable 'ping' not defined at a position that is outside the reported file (imports.py:176; confirmed by tests/python/imports/test_module_resolver.py:162-187).
  7. Top-level break; / continue; (outside any function) produce a bogus extra FS-PARSE-0010 Expected semicolon after statement alongside the correct SEM-0010 (repro s8/r6.fire / a2.fire). Inside functions only the SEM error appears.
  8. Same-scope redeclaration (duplicate: int32 = 1; duplicate: int32 = 2;) is reported as "already declared in an outer scope; shadowing not allowed" - wrong message for same scope (type_errors_comprehensive.fire:73).
  9. docs/reference/arrays.md:118-131 ("Nested Arrays ... not fully implemented", uses old int8[3][3] matrix = [...] syntax) vs. compiler rule "Array literals cannot directly contain arrays" pinned by 3 tests; the doc has no [PLANNED] marker on that section, which CLAUDE.md requires.
  10. Non-exported import yields only "Variable not defined" (no export-visibility diagnostic) - minor diagnostics-quality gap.

docs.title: Cross-cutting patterns worth fixing
docs.text:
• Missing import @firescript/std.io.println; in 4 old-style tests (type_mismatches, array_edge_invalid, control_flow_invalid, cast_and_generic l.39) makes print(...) a source of ~30 incidental annotations that pass for the wrong reason and would mask real regressions.

All paths relative to /home/alec/Programming/firescript/tests/sources/invalid/. 50 files, no //@ helper files in this slice. Observed with: python firescript/main.py --platform windows --arch x86_64 --check --message-format json . Scratch repros live in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-alec-Programming-firescript/2f6fea08-4b29-4fbd-9b67-4bb973797cf6/scratchpad/audit/x/ (not in repo). tests/python/* has no message/diagnostic-level coverage of any of these diagnostics (grepped), so the .fire files are the only coverage; redundancy is judged against other invalid/ files.

Key background facts found while auditing - Comments are ordinary tokens inside the parser (firescript/parser/base.py _COMMENT_TOKEN_TYPES, "stripped ad hoc by each parse loop"). The test-harness //~ comments therefore can CHANGE compiler behaviour: two tests below pin diagnostics that exist only because the annotation comment is there (see INCORRECT section). - Un-imported print/println yields FS-PARSE-0012 "Function 'print' is not defined", and that error SUPPRESSES the missing-semicolon error on the same statement (repro ms2 vs ms1), so legacy tests that call print without importing it are partly testing nothing.

syntax/syntax_errors.fire (INCORRECT + WEAK + REDUNDANT with syntax_comprehensive)
docs.text:
• 9 of 22 annotated diagnostics are "Function 'print' is not defined" (FS-PARSE-0012) because print is never imported. They are real errors but incidental noise unrelated to the test intent.
  • Line 4 print("-- invalid syntax: missing semicolons --") is missing a ; but that error is NOT reported: the undefined-function error masks it (repro: println("a")\nx: int32 = 1; without import -> only PARSE-0012; with import -> PARSE-0010 Expected semicolon after statement). So the first "missing semicolon" case is untested.
  • Line 28 else { print(1); } = control_flow/dangling_else_errors.fire (same FS-PARSE-0012 "Unexpected 'else' without matching 'if'"). Line 20 if 1) { and 24 while 1 < 2 { ~ loop_header_errors.fire / syntax_comprehensive.
